R0235.title: Refund Abuse Risk
R0235.definition: Users or organized groups exploit merchant or platform return, refund, and after-sales rules to obtain money, goods, or compensation through false reasons or evidence.

references.title: Typed Assessment of Buy-Genuine-Return-Fake Conduct - Supreme People’s Procuratorate
Returning Empty Parcels or Gifts to Fraudulently Obtain Online-Platform Refunds - Shandong High People’s Court
What Is Refund Fraud? How to Protect Your Business - Stripe

R0235.description:
Refund abuse occurs in merchant- or platform-controlled return, refund, refund-without-return, and after-sales compensation processes. Attackers may return empty parcels, cheaper substitutes, or damaged goods, fabricate delivery or defect evidence, or use linked accounts for repeated claims while retaining the product or consumed benefit.

Detection depends on consistency across orders, logistics, products, submitted evidence, and account history. It differs from R0139 friendly fraud, where a cardholder disputes a payment with the issuing bank and triggers a reversal outside the merchant's normal refund approval flow.
R0235.influence: Refund abuse causes losses of payments, goods, subsidies, and compensation, increases logistics verification and manual review costs, and undermines fair after-sales service.

observables: The same user or ring initiates high-frequency refunds accompanied by empty-package, swap-out, or item-mismatch evidence
Refund appeals cluster on related devices or delivery addresses
Fake sign-off anomalies or repeated appeal patterns are triggered in bulk
Refund-without-return, mismatched returns, or abnormal compensation spikes in a short window
Dispute handling shows an abnormally high share of users with historical anomalous behavior
